9397afbbdf14d1f13fe38facb428e18adabd7a60.summary: This page is an event listing for a BrightTalk webcast, 'The Sample: Beating the Malware Pinata', presented by Christopher Gardner of the Mandiant FLARE reverse engineering team and published 2022-05-05. It outlines talk topics such as analysing droppers, extracting payloads from process injection, and open-source intelligence. It is an event and marketing page, not a threat report, so no facts are recorded.

930cc42115fcbd879cf67403b12c3a3e4e347abe.summary: Researcher's archived 2022 analysis of a Korean-language HWP document lure, attributed by the author to North Korea-linked APT37 and to its ROKRAT operations. A malicious HWP OLE object runs a BAT script that launches PowerShell to load shellcode into memory through reflective DLL injection. The shellcode stager was offline, so the in-memory payload was not analysed. The attribution is the author's own judgement.

93e4ce0d8a68200769cb07c054f532f5ab7a7688.summary: Threatpost podcast transcript (published 2021-02-03) with Proofpoint's Sherrod DeGrippo about the law enforcement takedown of the Emotet malware. She reports no Emotet activity for about a week after the takedown and compares it with the TrickBot takedown, after which TrickBot returned within weeks. The discussion covers how takedowns work, the Ukraine location of the operators, and other malware families including Agent Tesla, Dridex and Ursnif. These are the speakers' opinions and predictions, not confirmed findings.

93b3d9455997fb6f28801426c0bcf0432eb87860.summary: Group-IB report on the Cobalt financial-crime group, covering 2016 to 2018. Europol reported the March 2018 arrest of its leader in Spain, but the report says attacks continued. It links Cobalt to thefts through bank card processing, ATMs and SWIFT, to supply-chain attacks on system integrators, and to a May 2018 phishing campaign impersonating an anti-virus vendor against banks in Russia and the CIS. It describes tools including the CobInt backdoor and a PetrWrap ransomware variant. It also presents a suspected joint operation with the Anunak/Carbanak group as a hypothesis.

hedges: The report says it is far too soon to dismiss Cobalt, despite the arrest of its leader.
The report says the group probably did not act alone in its early SWIFT attacks, given their sophistication.
Group-IB says it was confident Cobalt was involved in early SWIFT attacks, based on a unique loader.
The report says the link to Anunak/Carbanak is not the main reason to link the groups, and that a connection is high-probability.
